rationale: Zero pixels follow coordinates modulo 3: row residue 0 and column residue 1 or 2 become 8; row residue 2 and column residue 1 become 2, while column residue 2 becomes 5. Demonstration 2 shows these changes at (0,2), (3,1), (5,1), and (2,2), using zero-based coordinates.

Use own colour and the row's nonzero colour set. Rows containing only 2 fill zeros with 2; rows containing {2,3} change 3 to 4; rows containing {1,2,3} change zeros to 6 and 3 to 8. Demonstration 4 exhibits all three cases.

Row colour sets determine recolouring: {2} maps zeros to 7, {1,2} maps zeros to 4, {1,3} maps zeros to 7, and {1,2,3} maps 3 to 0. Demonstration 1 shows the {2}, {1,2}, and {1,2,3} cases; demonstration 3 shows {1,3}.

Own colour and coordinate parity determine output. On even rows, even-column 3 becomes 0, odd-column 0 becomes 4, and odd-column 2 becomes 1. On odd rows, even-column 2 becomes 4. Demonstrations 2 and 4 show these parity-specific changes.

On even rows, odd-column zeros become 2 and even-column 3 becomes 1. On odd rows, even-column zeros become 9 and even-column 2 becomes 6. Demonstration 10 directly shows zero-to-2, zero-to-9, and 2-to-6 changes.

Use own colour and nearest nonzero colours in the four cardinal directions. Demonstrations 7 and 8 change a zero with nearest colours (up absent, down 1, left 2, right absent) to 6. Demonstration 6 changes (2,5), with nearest colours (1, absent, 1, absent), to 1.

Use own colour with both row and column nonzero sets. Demonstration 3 changes (2,0) from 1 to 6 where the row has {1,2,3} and column has {1,2,3}; (2,1) changes 2 to 3 where the row has {1,2,3} and column has {2,3}. Demonstration 4 also changes a zero to 6 where the row has {1,3} and column is empty.

Nearest cardinal nonzero colours determine zero recolouring. Demonstration 1 changes (0,1) to 6 with neighbours (up absent, down 2, left 2, right absent); demonstration 2 repeats that key at (1,2). Demonstration 7 changes top-row zeros to 3 with neighbours (absent, 2, absent, 3).

Zeros on rows congruent to 1 modulo 3 become 3 in columns congruent to 1. Zeros on rows congruent to 2 become 7, 9, or 1 for column residues 0, 1, or 2. Demonstration 2 shows the full 7,9,1 pattern in row 5 and zero-to-3 changes in rows 1 and 4.

Every 2 on an even row becomes 0; 1 on an even row and even column becomes 9; zero on an odd row and odd column becomes 1. Demonstration 3 shows all three changes, while demonstration 4 shows repeated odd-row zero-to-1 filling.
